pages.transcription:
Stefan is just busy working, so I send
the letter without word from him.

7 Bamapo Road
Ossining, N.Y.
4.7.41

Dear Manna & Manfred,
I had the idea of writing you the very
first day of our arrival here as long letter, but the heat
made me lazy and took all my energy. We are now quite
settled until the end of August and I thoroughly enjoy being
in a house again and even the housekeeping. The maid is
a great treat for me and I almost feel like the time
we got Rhoda. Why I should feel like that I do not know
myself for I certainly did not work hard or a lot in the
hotel, and the Wyndham, being a small and mostly residential
hotel is not as impersonal as most of them. Anyhow, I am
glad to be here and out of New York which was already very
hot, sticky and smelly. The situation of our house here is in
certain ways very similar to Mrs Leckie's house in Bath.
It is not the house itself which is much smaller and alto-
gether different, but its position on a hill with a steep
driveway, and a very awkward angle to the garage, but a
good garage so that I involuntarily thought when we
saw it: that will be a good garage when Manfred comes
with his car. Thinking of that house in Bath I miss
Martha much, of course - not to speak of your visits. But
we can visit Eva instead and Monday I shall take her
to New York (we both have to go to the dentist and I
must get my weekly supply of bacterias injected) and I
shall keep her with us for a day or two. I don't think
much longer, for there is nothing whatsoever to be done
or seen in Ossining. Sing-Sing is in Ossining, but one rather
tries to forget this fact. - Did I write you that Miss Baker
came to see me in New York? Her visit was interesting for me,
but I was amazed how talkative she was and how naive she
still is. She still was not quite resigned to the fact that she
could not go to England just for the summer holidays - this
in a time where it is impossible to obtain any kind of passage
except for solid and urgent business or political reasons. - A few
days ago I sent a small parcel, mainly sweets to Manfred, hoping
that it will eventually reach him. I also sent one to Ursula whose
birthday must be very soon. A small amount of duty may have
to be paid for both. I also sent you 'Life' and 'Vogue' by ordinary
mail.

[Randnotiz links, von unten nach oben geschrieben:]
I was not quite sure which kind of magazine interests you, whether literary, fashion,
or more serious ones. Let me know please and please send me once in a while
a newspaper or magazine which might be of interest for me. I should love to see an
Evening Standard. Love and kisses.
pages.notes: Handschriftlicher Brief von Lotte Zweig. Die Tinte ist blau/violett. Die Randnotiz ist vertikal am linken Rand geschrieben.
